**A recent absence of a negative event is not a mature positive label.** If chargebacks or defaults arrive 30–90 days later, today's unlabeled transaction may eventually become a confirmed adverse outcome. Training immediately on “no event yet” as a final negative creates systematic label bias. [1](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/rules-of-ml)

**Separate feature time, observation time, and label maturity.** Store features as available when the prediction was made. Track the outcome window and when labels become sufficiently mature for the chosen target. Backfill late outcomes idempotently and retain dataset versions so a model can be traced to the labels it actually used.

Use a mature-label training baseline, then consider delay-aware or survival-based methods if recency is important and their assumptions are justified. Early proxy labels can support monitoring, but should not silently replace the final business outcome without validation.

**Retraining and deployment are separate gates.** A pipeline may train candidates on schedule while waiting for reliable evaluation before promotion. Compare on time-separated, appropriately matured cohorts and keep a champion model with rollback. Drift alerts can trigger investigation without automatically shipping a newly fitted model.

Monitor label arrival distributions, missing outcomes, and selection bias in manually reviewed cases. A change in reporting delay can look like improved performance before labels catch up. Dashboards should expose maturity so the team does not celebrate an apparent gain caused by incomplete observation.

**Technical details and references.**

Separate decision time, feature-availability time, and label-maturity time. Train on cohorts whose outcomes have matured, using point-in-time features; do not silently label unresolved cases negative. Version each label snapshot because chargebacks or defaults can arrive late or be revised. [1](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/rules-of-ml) [2](https://docs.feast.dev/getting-started/concepts/point-in-time-joins)

Monitor fast proxy signals for data/serving failures, but validate retraining decisions against mature outcomes. If early learning is essential, model censoring or delay explicitly and verify assumptions. Use rolling temporal evaluation with a gap matching the label horizon and assess recent matured cohorts separately.

A promotion pipeline should check quality, calibration, important slices, feature parity, and rollback readiness. Retraining more often cannot remove a 90-day information delay; it may simply reuse mostly unchanged mature data or amplify biased provisional labels.
